We produced an initial alloy ingot with a chemical composition of Nb–16Si–25Ti–8Hf–2Cr–2Al (at.-%) using vacuum arc melting in a water-cooled copper crucible.
The alloy was remelted five times and annealed at 1200°C for 10 h under a high vacuum (10−5 torr) atmosphere to homogenise its chemical concentration.
The alloy ingot was annealed at 600°C for 2h in a 100% H2 atmosphere for hydrogenation.

Then, the hydrogenated ingot was pulverised by a ball-milling with a stainless steel milling container and tungsten carbide balls as the milling media. The alloy powder to tungsten carbide ball ratio was 1:5 by weigh and the ball-milling was performed for 1 h at a rotation speed of 200 rev min−1.
After milling, the powders were sieved by using meshes ranging in size from 25 to 63μm.
Afterward, the powders were annealed at 600°C for 2h under a high vacuum (10−5 torr) atmosphere for dehydrogenation.
